25: strictly after ``after``, with seconds and microseconds zero. If nothing
26: matches within the next five years (e.g. ``0 0 30 2 *``), it raises
27: ``ValueError``.
28: """
29: 
30: from __future__ import annotations
31: 
32: import re
33: from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
34: 
35: _NUMERIC = re.compile(r"[0-9]+")
36: 
37: _MONTH_NAMES = {
38:     "JAN": 1,
39:     "FEB": 2,
40:     "MAR": 3,
41:     "APR": 4,
42:     "MAY": 5,
43:     "JUN": 6,
44:     "JUL": 7,
45:     "AUG": 8,
46:     "SEP": 9,
47:     "OCT": 10,
48:     "NOV": 11,
49:     "DEC": 12,
50: }
51: 
52: _WEEKDAY_NAMES = {
53:     "SUN": 0,
54:     "MON": 1,
55:     "TUE": 2,
56:     "WED": 3,
57:     "THU": 4,
58:     "FRI": 5,
59:     "SAT": 6,
60: }
61: 
62: 
63: def _parse_value(
64:     token: str,
65:     label: str,
66:     minimum: int,
67:     maximum: int,
68:     names: dict[str, int] | None,
69: ) -> int:
70:     """Parse one numeric or named value from a field."""
71:     if names is not None:
72:         value = names.get(token.upper())
73:         if value is not None:
74:             return value
75: 
76:     if _NUMERIC.fullmatch(token) is None:
77:         raise ValueError(f"invalid {label} value: {token!r}")
78: 
79:     value = int(token)
80:     if value < minimum or value > maximum:
81:         raise ValueError(
82:             f"{label} value {value} is outside {minimum}-{maximum}"
83:         )
84:     return value
85: 
86: 
87: def _parse_field(
88:     text: str,
89:     label: str,
90:     minimum: int,
91:     maximum: int,
92:     names: dict[str, int] | None = None,
93: ) -> frozenset[int]:
94:     """Expand one cron field into the set of values it matches."""
95:     values: set[int] = set()
96: 
97:     for item in text.split(","):
98:         if item == "":
99:             raise ValueError(f"empty item in {label} field")
100: 
101:         pieces = item.split("/")
102:         if len(pieces) > 2:
103:             raise ValueError(f"malformed {label} item: {item!r}")
104: 
105:         base = pieces[0]
106:         has_step = len(pieces) == 2
107:         step = 1
108:         if has_step:
109:             step_text = pieces[1]
110:             if _NUMERIC.fullmatch(step_text) is None or int(step_text) == 0:
111:                 raise ValueError(f"invalid step in {label} item: {item!r}")
112:             step = int(step_text)
113: 
114:         if base == "*":
115:             start, stop = minimum, maximum
116:         elif "-" in base:
117:             bounds = base.split("-")
118:             if len(bounds) != 2:
119:                 raise ValueError(f"malformed {label} item: {item!r}")
120:             start = _parse_value(bounds[0], label, minimum, maximum, names)
121:             stop = _parse_value(bounds[1], label, minimum, maximum, names)
122:             if start > stop:
123:                 raise ValueError(f"reversed range in {label} item: {item!r}")
124:         else:
125:             start = _parse_value(base, label, minimum, maximum, names)
126:             if not has_step:
127:                 values.add(start)
128:                 continue
129:             stop = maximum
130: 
131:         values.update(range(start, stop + 1, step))
132: 
133:     if label == "day of week":
134:         # Numeric 7 is Sunday; normalise it to 0 so matching is uniform.
135:         values = {value % 7 for value in values}
136: 
137:     return frozenset(values)
138: 
139: 
140: def _parse(
141:     expression: str,
142: ) -> tuple[
143:     frozenset[int],
144:     frozenset[int],
145:     frozenset[int],
146:     frozenset[int],
147:     frozenset[int],
148:     bool,
149:     bool,
150: ]:
151:     """Parse a whole expression into field value sets and restriction flags."""
152:     if not isinstance(expression, str):
153:         raise ValueError("cron expression must be a string")
154: 
155:     fields = expression.split()
156:     if len(fields) != 5:
157:         raise ValueError(
158:             f"expected 5 cron fields, found {len(fields)}"
159:         )
160: 
161:     minutes = _parse_field(fields[0], "minute", 0, 59)
162:     hours = _parse_field(fields[1], "hour", 0, 23)
163:     days = _parse_field(fields[2], "day of month", 1, 31)
164:     months = _parse_field(fields[3], "month", 1, 12, _MONTH_NAMES)
165:     weekdays = _parse_field(fields[4], "day of week", 0, 7, _WEEKDAY_NAMES)
166: 
167:     # Vixie cron's rule depends on whether the raw field text is exactly "*".
168:     # In particular, "*/1" counts as restricted.
169:     day_restricted = fields[2] != "*"
170:     weekday_restricted = fields[4] != "*"
171: 
172:     return (
173:         minutes,
174:         hours,
175:         days,
176:         months,
177:         weekdays,
178:         day_restricted,
179:         weekday_restricted,
180:     )
181: 
182: 
183: def _day_matches(
184:     day: date,
185:     days: frozenset[int],
186:     weekdays: frozenset[int],
187:     day_restricted: bool,
188:     weekday_restricted: bool,
189: ) -> bool:
190:     """Whether the calendar date satisfies the day-of-month/day-of-week rule."""
191:     day_ok = day.day in days
192:     # datetime.weekday() is Monday=0; cron is Sunday=0.
193:     weekday_ok = (day.weekday() + 1) % 7 in weekdays
194: 
195:     if day_restricted and weekday_restricted:
196:         return day_ok or weekday_ok
197:     return day_ok and weekday_ok
198: 
199: 
200: def _five_years_after(moment: datetime) -> datetime:
201:     """``moment`` plus five years, clamping Feb 29 when needed."""
202:     target_year = moment.year + 5
203:     if target_year > datetime.max.year:
204:         return datetime.max.replace(tzinfo=moment.tzinfo)
205: 
206:     try:
207:         return moment.replace(year=target_year)
208:     except ValueError:
209:         # Only Feb 29 can fail here; clamp to Feb 28.
210:         return moment.replace(year=target_year, day=28)
211: 
212: 
213: def next_run(expression: str, after: datetime) -> datetime:
214:     """The first time after ``after`` that ``expression`` fires."""
215:     (
216:         minutes,
217:         hours,
218:         days,
219:         months,
220:         weekdays,
221:         day_restricted,
222:         weekday_restricted,
223:     ) = _parse(expression)
224: 
225:     try:
226:         # The next whole minute is always strictly after ``after``, even when
227:         # ``after`` already lies exactly on a minute boundary.
228:         start = after.replace(second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(minutes=1)
229:     except (OverflowError, ValueError) as exc:
230:         raise ValueError("no matching time within five years") from exc
231: 
232:     limit = _five_years_after(after)
233: 
234:     sorted_hours = sorted(hours)
235:     sorted_minutes = sorted(minutes)
236:     start_date = start.date()
237:     end_date = limit.date()
238:     current = start_date
239:     one_day = timedelta(days=1)
240: 
241:     while True:

243:             current, days, weekdays, day_restricted, weekday_restricted
244:         ):
245:             if current == start_date:
246:                 first_hour, first_minute = start.hour, start.minute
247:             else:
248:                 first_hour = first_minute = 0
249: 
250:             for hour in sorted_hours:
251:                 if hour < first_hour:
252:                     continue
253:                 for minute in sorted_minutes:
254:                     if hour == first_hour and minute < first_minute:
255:                         continue
256: 
257:                     candidate = after.replace(
258:                         year=current.year,
259:                         month=current.month,
260:                         day=current.day,
261:                         hour=hour,
262:                         minute=minute,
263:                         second=0,
264:                         microsecond=0,
265:                     )
266:                     if candidate > limit:
267:                         raise ValueError("no matching time within five years")
268:                     return candidate
269: 
270:         if current >= end_date:
271:             break
272:         current += one_day
273: 
274:     raise ValueError("no matching time within five years")
